VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed answer f(n) = (n+7)/5 is probably not the intended one. The known sharp threshold for rainbow C₄ in edge-colored triangle-free graphs is (n+6)/5, stated with "≥". The proposed solution's own sharpness claim conflicts with that: it says a blow-up of C₅ on n = 5m−1 vertices has minimum color degree m+1 = (n+6)/5 and no rainbow C₄. If that example were valid, δ^c ≥ (n+6)/5 would not suffice, contradicting the literature bound. So the example is likely flawed, and I did not verify it.

The two expressions are not interchangeable under "≥". (n+7)/5 and (n+6)/5 have different ceilings exactly when n ≡ 4 (mod 5). The equivalence to "δ^c > (n+6)/5" holds for integer color degrees, but the problem asks for the bound in the form (n+a)/b with ≥, so a = 6 is the expected answer.

CONFIDENCE: 3
